# Philippines

Wealth gradients in fertility and mortality: the values for an OG-Core calibration, followed by the estimates they are based on. Terms are defined in the [glossary](../glossary.md).

## Values for OG-Core

| OG-Core input | Wealth gradient | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `fert_gradient` | −0.99, by age as below | DHS 2022, TFR, plus [age offsets](../methods/fertility-by-age.md) |
| `infmort_gradient` | −1.60 | DHS 2022, infant mortality rate |
| `mort_gradient` | −0.92 (95% prediction interval −1.41 to −0.44) | [general gradient](../methods/general-gradient.md) at GNI per capita of $4,470 (about 2024) |
| `imm_pctiles` | not provided | — |

Values are [wealth gradients](../glossary.md#wealth-gradient). Before they are passed to OG-Core, each is divided by 100 × (1 − p), where p is OG-Core's rate at that age ([details](../methods/ogcore-units.md)).

**Fertility gradient by age of mother** (`fert_gradient`; ages below 15 use the 15–19 value, ages 50 and above the 45–49 value):

| 15–19 | 20–24 | 25–29 | 30–34 | 35–39 | 40–44 | 45–49 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| −1.76 | −1.09 | −0.78 | −0.66 | −0.89 | −1.38 | −1.97 |

## Estimates

### Demographic and Health Surveys

Latest survey with a complete wealth-quintile breakdown ([`gradient_library_latest.csv`](../../data/gradient_library_latest.csv); earlier surveys in `gradient_library.csv`).

| Indicator | Survey | Lowest | Second | Middle | Fourth | Highest | Low/high ratio | Gradient |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Total fertility rate (births per woman) | 2022 | 3.1 | 2.2 | 2 | 1.5 | 1.4 | 2.21 | −0.99 |
| Infant mortality rate (per 1,000 live births) | 2022 | 24 | 17 | 23 | 11 | 6 | 4.00 | −1.60 |
| Under-five mortality rate (per 1,000 live births) | 2022 | 35 | 23 | 25 | 13 | 8 | 4.38 | −1.76 |

## Notes

- No census or survey with a household-deaths module is available (the DHS surveys record deaths of children only), so adult mortality uses the general gradient (value in the table above). Fertility and infant mortality come from the 2022 NDHS.
